interest: Shows 1935 US research into Japan's mining law restrictions, tied to Japanese objections over the Philippine draft constitution.
overview: Hull asks Tokyo about Japan's mining-law restrictions on foreigners amid Philippine constitution talks; Grew reports only mining and subsidy laws bar foreign business activity.

subfiles.about: Inquiry to the Tokyo Embassy regarding Japanese legal provisions restricting the development of natural resources by foreign nationals.
subfiles.summary: Hull asks Tokyo to report on Japan's Mining Law Article 5 and any other restrictions on foreign resource exploitation.
subfiles.title: Telegram from Department of State to Tokyo Embassy regarding restrictions on foreign exploitation of natural resources

subfiles.about: Internal research note quoting Japanese mining law and legal commentary on alien rights regarding natural resources and territorial waters.
subfiles.summary: Memo quotes Japan's mining law barring foreigners from mining rights, and notes alien exclusion from territorial fishing and hunting.
subfiles.title: Division of Far Eastern Affairs note on Japanese Mining Law and alien rights

subfiles.about: Report from Ambassador Grew on legal restrictions affecting foreign business enterprises and natural resource development in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Grew reports only mining and subsidy laws restrict foreign business in Japan, finding no other specific barriers.
subfiles.title: Telegram from Ambassador Grew to Secretary of State regarding legal restrictions on foreigners

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet linking inquiries on Japanese natural resource laws to Japanese government proposals regarding the Philippine draft constitution.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference links Japan's foreign resource-exploitation restrictions to Japanese suggestions on the Philippine draft constitution.
subfiles.title: Cross-reference sheet regarding natural resource inquiries and the Philippine draft constitution
